stories.label: Recovering From Errors
stories.title: Can an Agent Recover and Still Finish?
stories.instruction: Excavate three sites, date the artifacts, and place the red flag at the oldest site.
stories.takeaway: An early error need not end an episode. Opus 5.5 recovers from two initial code errors and finishes in seven rounds; DeepSeek-1017 reaches a partial score of 0.5, then uses its remaining rounds without completing the task.
stories.question: What matters after a mistake?
stories.answer: Whether subsequent actions change the task state. Watch the native score rise after Opus collects the tools, dates the artifacts, and places the flag; compare the stalled final rounds of DeepSeek-1017.

stories.label: Finishing the Sequence
stories.title: Does More Motion Mean More Progress?
stories.instruction: Lift the blue block from the sliding cabinet, put it in the drawer, retrieve it, stack it, and switch off the light.
stories.takeaway: On sequence 0526, Opus 5.5 completes all five subgoals with 338 action submissions. Gemini makes hundreds of submissions but completes none before its token budget ends.
stories.question: Which progress signal should we trust?
stories.answer: The native sequence verifier. Motion, a valid tool call and a completed subgoal are different events. Open a round to inspect the requested action, current subgoal and returned state.

stories.label: Calls vs. Completion
stories.title: A Successful Call Is Not a Successful Task.
stories.takeaway: Fable 5.1 reaches the native drawer-success condition in 20 rounds. Sol uses all 24 rounds without completing it. The trace separates successful tool execution from the environment’s task check.
stories.question: Where does execution stop translating into progress?
stories.answer: Inspect observations, target grounding and end-effector moves alongside their returned feedback. Tool “ok” reports that a call ran; the final native verifier decides whether the drawer task is complete.

stories.label: Meeting Every Condition
stories.title: One Condition Is Not the Whole Goal.
stories.instruction: Clean the soap bar and place it in the bathtub.
stories.takeaway: Gemini completes this task within eight rounds. DeepSeek-1017 also uses eight rounds but finishes with only one of three goal conditions met. Finding and moving an object is only part of the instruction.
stories.question: Why can plausible actions still fail?
stories.answer: ALFRED checks the requested final state, including the cleaning condition. Inspect the per-round goal count and the returned object state, rather than judging success from movement alone.

stories.label: The Cost of a Decision
stories.title: Fewer Decisions Do Not Always Mean Less Time.
stories.instruction: Find the chair and move until the body is touching the target, then stop.
stories.takeaway: All three recorded agents complete this navigation task. Astra uses 18 rounds in about 471 seconds, Sol 17 in 669 seconds, and DeepSeek-1017 65 in 406 seconds. Round count and elapsed time capture different costs.
stories.question: How should execution efficiency be compared?
stories.answer: Read task completion, environment steps, model calls, tokens and elapsed time together. This is a navigation episode; it does not change the separate sitting-task result.

stories.label: When Budgets Run Out
stories.title: Which Resource Runs Out First?
stories.instruction: Outfit a basic toolbox with the required tools.
stories.takeaway: None of these eight recorded episodes passes the native completion check. Some stop at the token limit and others at the round limit, with recorded durations ranging from about 12 to 133 minutes.
stories.question: Would a longer time limit alone fix the failure?
stories.answer: These episodes already have a 180-minute time ceiling. Their recorded stopping conditions are token or round limits. More allowed time alone does not remove those limits; whether a larger overall budget helps requires another experiment.

stories.label: Contact and Precision
stories.title: The Last Contact Can Remain Unsolved.
stories.instruction: Insert the charger into the socket.
stories.takeaway: Qwen Max and Qwen 397B each reach 400 native steps without task success. DeepSeek-1017 stops after 32 model rounds and 385 native steps. Motion must satisfy the insertion criterion to count.
stories.question: What does the final state establish?
stories.answer: The native verifier reports no successful insertion in these three episodes. Use the action parameters and feedback to inspect the attempts; the recordings do not isolate a single causal explanation.
